name: Diun
description: Docker Image Update Notifier: headless, notification-only checks for newer image versions (ntfy, mail, Discord, webhooks, ...).

choiceGroup.note: Headless alternative to What's Up Docker (which has a web interface). One of the two is enough; neither updates anything.

privileges.explain: A socket proxy on Diun's private network gets the Docker socket read-only and allows only reading containers, images and events (no POST, exec or delete). Diun itself never sees the socket.

security: Notification only: Diun never pulls, updates, restarts or removes containers.
Notifier credentials (mail password, webhook URLs) go into config/diun.yml, which is readable by your Windows account only.

notes: Headless: no web interface, nothing to sign in to.

limitations: Reads Docker through a read-only socket proxy; it notifies only and never pulls or updates anything.
Without a notifier configured in config/diun.yml, results appear only in its log.

update.notes: Diun keeps its state in the data volume; updates change only the image.

volumes.name: data
volumes.description: Diun's database of images already seen.

volumes.name: config
volumes.description: diun.yml: schedule, Docker provider and notifiers.

files.content:
# Diun configuration (https://crazymax.dev/diun/config/). Written once at installation; your edits are kept.
# Diun only reports newer image versions. It never pulls, updates or restarts anything.
db:
  path: /data/diun.db
watch:
  workers: 10
  schedule: "0 */6 * * *"
  jitter: 30s
  firstCheckNotif: false
  runOnStartup: true
providers:
  docker:
    endpoint: tcp://{{service:socket-proxy}}:2375
    watchByDefault: true
    watchStopped: false
# Notifications: uncomment one or more notifiers, fill them in, then restart Diun (Restart on the Installed apps page).
# Without a notifier, Diun writes what it finds to its log.
#notif:
#  ntfy:
#    endpoint: https://ntfy.sh
#    topic: choose-a-private-topic
#  discord:
#    webhookURL: https://discord.com/api/webhooks/...
#  mail:
#    host: smtp.example.com
#    port: 587
#    username: you@example.com
#    password: your-app-password
#    from: diun@example.com
#    to:
#      - you@example.com

testStatus.notes: Installed in isolation: headless, log check, backup and restore (2026-11-16).
